nodes.summary: Superposition (Kingman 1993, §2.2): the sum of two independent Poisson processes of rates `r₁` and `r₂` is a Poisson process of rate `r₁ + r₂`. Independence is of the two processes as random paths.
nodes.title: Superposition

nodes.summary: The counting process of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrivals has nondecreasing paths almost surely (the arrival times tend to infinity almost surely, so every arrival set in `[0, t]` is finite).
nodes.title: Counting process has nondecreasing paths almost surely

nodes.summary: The counting process of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrivals starts at `0` almost surely (all interarrival times are positive almost surely).
nodes.title: Counting process starts at zero almost surely

nodes.summary: The `n`-th arrival time `S n = T 0 + ⋯ + T (n - 1)` of the interarrival times `T`.
nodes.title: Arrival times from interarrival times

nodes.summary: The counting process of the interarrival times `T`: `count T t ω` is the number of arrivals `n ≥ 1` with `S n ≤ t`. When that set is infinite (a null event for exponential interarrivals of positive rate) `Set.ncard` returns `0`.
nodes.title: Counting process of interarrival times

nodes.summary: The `(n + 1)`-th arrival time of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrivals has the Gamma (Erlang) law with shape `n + 1` and rate `r` (Karlin–Taylor 1975, §4.2).
nodes.title: Arrival times of exponential interarrivals are Erlang

nodes.summary: The increments of the counting process of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrivals over consecutive intervals `(t i, t (i + 1)]` are independent with the Poisson laws of means `r (t (i + 1) - t i)`: the increment vector has the product law (Kingman 1993, ch. 4; Karlin–Taylor 1975, ch. 4).
nodes.title: Independent Poisson increments of the counting process

nodes.summary: The number of arrivals in `[0, t]` of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrivals has the Poisson law of mean `r t` (Karlin–Taylor 1975, §4.2, Theorem 2.1).
nodes.title: Arrival counts of exponential interarrivals are Poisson

nodes.summary: Exponential interarrivals give a Poisson process (Kingman 1993, ch. 4; Karlin–Taylor 1975, ch. 4): the counting process of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrival times is a Poisson process of rate `r`.
nodes.title: Exponential interarrivals give a Poisson process

nodes.summary: `N : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℕ` is a Poisson process of rate `r` under `P` (Kingman 1993, ch. 4; Karlin–Taylor 1975, ch. 4): `N 0 = 0` and the paths are nondecreasing almost surely, the increments over consecutive intervals are independent, and for `s ≤ t` the increment `N t - N s` has the Poisson law of mean `r (t - s)`.
nodes.title: Poisson process

nodes.summary: Thinning (Kingman 1993, §5.1; Karlin–Taylor 1975, §4.1): keeping each point of a Poisson process of rate `r` independently with probability `p`, independently of the process, gives a Poisson process of rate `p r`. The marks `B i` are i.i.d. with `P(B i) = p` and independent of `N` as a random path.
nodes.title: Thinning

nodes.summary: The thinning of `N` by the marks `B`: the number of indices `i < N t` with `B i`, i.e. the number of points of `N` in `[0, t]` that are kept when the `i`-th point (in time order, from `0`) is kept iff `B i`.
nodes.title: Thinning of a Poisson process

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
